item.title: The Ripple Effect of Going for It
item.description: Can you learn to captain a yacht at 62 and turn it into a world-traveling lifestyle? Absolutely! Below, Sine Maria shares a first-hand account of her family’s latest charter with Dream Yacht in the Balearic Islands. Read on for an inspiring look at courage, partnership, and what happens when you say yes to a new adventure on the water. The Ripple Effect of Going for It On breaking into worlds you weren’t born into, and what happens when you actually do the thing. By: Good Life Designed and Sine Maria If there’s one thing I’ve learned from my mom, it’s that life has so much to offer and the limit of your world is only limited by your ability to keep expanding. In the middle of the pandemic, as part of our collective pause, she and I decided to go through the whole Good Life Designed program together again. It was through that process that she decided she wanted to be closer to nature, swim more, and learn how to sail. She didn’t grow up around sailing, knew it was costly and a bit of a boys club, but always admired the access it gave those who knew how. That hobby could take you anywhere in the world. The world of sailing requires a unique blend of resources, courage, technical education, practice, and willing crew members to go along for the ride and be there while you figure things out on your first trips alone. It thrives behind heavy yacht club doors that some are born with access into – but most don’t even know exist. The dream of being certified as a sailor has an even smaller niche- attracting those who thrive on the pressure to read and respond to the chaos of the elements at sea while holding the responsibility of passengers’ lives in their hands. Now that I have experienced the reward that comes with that kind of responsibility – I see the draw. Breaking Into a World You Weren’t Born Into I tried to look into data about women certified sailors but couldn’t find any credible data because no one seems to be particularly interested in that stat – however I can tell you there aren’t many. Sailing, just due to the nature of it, the time it requires, the unease that comes with the experience, especially as you’re getting your first solo trips under your belt, is enough to send anyone right over the edge. It’s heady, it’s overwhelming, it’s complicated, it’s technical, and it feels uncertain and dangerous before you’re skilled and experienced enough to feel truly comfortable and at ease on the water. When Pernille got the ping to learn to sail, the biggest question was how, as a 62-year-old woman, was she going to do it. She tried visiting yacht clubs but as someone who wasn’t interested in the social component and was really looking for the technical skills to captain her own ship, it didn’t feel like the best place to spend her time or money. The classes and day sail opportunities to get out on the water were nice, but if she really wanted to learn everything she needed to, she needed something different. She came across Nautilus Sailing, a week-long course in the Sea of Cortez that would teach you everything you need to know about sailing and cap off the week with a test that would certify you to sail on your own anywhere in the world. My dad at the time was in the most stressful period of his career, navigating his independent school and their 400 families through Covid. Using his coveted spring break to learn to navigate another set of uncharted territories felt not quite like the vacation he needed. But he took a leap of his own and joined her anyway. They spent a week disconnected from everything to focus on learning the thing that would later give them access to the life they live now – barely imaginable to them then. Heading out on what feel like once-in-a-lifetime week long sailing experiences all over the world with friends and family. item.title: French Polynesia Cabin Cruise: The Floating Boutique Hotel for Effortless Island Hopping
item.description: Imagine waking up in a comfortable suite aboard a premium catamaran. You stretch out on crisp sheets and wonder what spectacular view is awaiting you today. Will it be the majestic twin peaks of Bora Bora or the white sand beaches and tropical jungles of Huahine? You step on deck and sniff the air: today’s port is actually the vanilla-scented shores of Taha’a. That’s what life is like aboard a French Polynesia cabin cruise. Every day, you get to go on a new adventure. At night, you rest and relax in the comfort of a spacious cabin aboard a shared catamaran charter. For many travelers, the freedom to visit multiple destinations rather than be confined to a single resort makes a cabin cruise a much better option than a typical holiday on land. What Is a French Polynesia Cabin Cruise? A French Polynesia catamaran cruise or cabin cruise is a travel option where you book a private cabin with its own attached bathroom on a catamaran. Instead of chartering an entire yacht yourself, you share the vessel with a small group of other travelers. How Cabin Cruises Work The catamaran operates much like a small-scale cruise ship but with a personalized touch. Your captain navigates the islands, and an onboard steward prepares your meals. This vacation style eliminates the stress of trip planning, sailing logistics, and meal preparation. And since vessels are shared among travelers, cabin cruises are more affordable than booking Tahiti yacht charters . Why It Feels Like a Floating Boutique Hotel Unlike massive cruise ships that carry thousands of passengers, a catamaran hosts between 8 and 12 guests. This creates an intimate atmosphere, similar to that of a small hotel, except you also get to experience different destinations and activities every day. In French Polynesia, our cabin cruises are offered on the Bali 5.4, Lagoon 620, and the Fountaine Pajot Ipanema 58, each accommodating 12 guests. Comfort and Convenience: What Is a Cabin Cruise Like Onboard? Life aboard a cabin charter is defined by relaxation and comfort. Your catamaran features decks, shaded outdoor dining areas, and a forward trampoline net. This net is a great spot to lounge as the islands glide by. No jostling for sunbathing space on crowded beaches or lining up to rent gear from stands along the shore. You can get all the sun you want on deck, and the cruise includes the use of water sports equipment. You can step directly off the yacht’s transom steps into the water, swim, snorkel, or kayak to your heart’s content. Island Hopping Without Repacking or Airport Transfers With 118 islands and atolls spread across an area as vast as Western Europe, French Polynesia island hopping is all about discovering the unique character of each destination. However, having your base camp be a hotel or resort limits your options. It also means you have to go through a drawn-out process of getting there before you can visit each different island. Traditional travelers must pack their suitcases, check out of their resorts, take a taxi to the airport, wait in security lines, and fly to the next island, only to repeat the check-in process. Meanwhile, on Tahiti cabin cruises , you unpack your bags once on arrival. While you relax on deck or sleep in your cabin, the catamaran moves you between Tahiti and other destinations like Huahine, Raiatea, Taha’a, and Bora Bora. A Tahiti cabin charter eliminates the need for regional flights and ferry schedules, saving you both travel stress and vacation time. Space, Food, Privacy, and Seasickness: Honest Answers Before booking a sailing trip, it is normal to have a few questions about how things work on a boat. Here is what daily life aboard your shared luxury catamaran looks like. Space: Yacht cabins are smaller than hotel rooms, but they’re just as well-appointed. item.title: How to charter a yacht for vacation
item.description: If you’re wondering how to charter a yacht for vacation, or want to know about the different types of charters, then you’ve come to the right place. A sailing vacation provides plenty of time to explore new islands, relax on beautiful beaches and snorkel in tropical seas while spending quality time with your family and friends. Combining adventure with relaxation, it’s a great way to spend your much-needed vacation. Sound interesting? Discover how you can charter a yacht for vacation with us. 1 Decide where you want to charter We have the widest choice of destinations, in fact we have more than 60 exquisite locations where you can hire a yacht for a vacation, including the Caribbean, Bahamas, Indian Ocean, Pacific, Asia and the Mediterranean to name a few. We choose our bases carefully. Close to airports : Our bases are close to major international hubs and our friendly and welcoming base teams can organize transfers for you Local knowledge : Each destination on our website has useful information to help you prepare, including a guide to the local base and area Discover our exciting destinations . 2 Decide which yacht charter type is right for you If you are wondering how to charter a yacht, you also need to decide which charter type is right for you. We offer bareboat yacht charters, skippered charters, by the cabin charters and crewed yacht charters. Bareboat yacht charters for sailors: If you have sailing experience, you can hire a yacht and sail yourself with our bareboat yacht charters. You can even sail one way from some locations. Unsure if you have the right sailing qualifications? Read our guide, are you qualified for a bareboat yacht charter ? Explore our bareboat yacht charter fleet . Skippered charters for vacations with a difference: If you want to experience a sailing vacation and can’t sail, it’s likely you’re questioning how to rent a yacht. All you need to do is hire a skipper to sail the boat for you with our skippered yacht charters. No sailing experience is needed. The skipper will sail your yacht, look after your safety, track the weather and advise you on your route. Learn more about our skippered charters . By the cabin charters for hassle-free, exciting vacations : Reserve a stateroom with private bathroom and explore 15+ wonderful destinations worldwide with our hassle-free, organized cruises. All you need to do is book your flights, arrive and relax. Our experienced captain will sail the boat while a professional chef will prepare all your meals for you. Discover our by the cabin charters and read our FAQs . Crewed charters for the ultimate luxury experience: If you’re looking for luxury, all-inclusive sailing vacations, our crewed charters offer five-star service from a professional crew on board our private yachts. Relax with your guests and enjoy a completely personalized experience tailored to your preferences. You don’t need sailing experience, just an idea of your dream vacation. Experience our crewed charters and read our FAQs . Sabbatical yacht charters for adventure seekers: For those searching for an adventure of a lifetime, our sabbatical yacht charters are designed for bluewater sailing enthusiasts wanting to explore the world. Our sabbatical fleet is kitted out for voyages up to 12-months. Our long-term charter service includes training, support during your voyage and maintenance at our bases worldwide. Find out more about sabbatical yacht charters and read our FAQs . 3 Find your dream yacht When looking for your dream yacht, the following points in our how to charter a yacht guide are important to consider. Our boats are priced according to their age, features, destination and season you are sailing. For advice on how to keep your charter affordable, read our guide on how much bareboat yacht charters cost under the FAQs tab . Short on time? We can find your dream yacht for you. Contact our team . item.title: New BALI Catamarans arriving in the Seychelles
item.description: As Dream Yacht’s first base location and founding sailing destination nearly 25 years ago, the Seychelles Islands hold a place of honor in the hearts and minds of our Dream Yacht Worldwide charter team. Now we’re pleased to announce the arrival of two brand new catamarans soon to be available for charter in this very special island paradise. The new yachts, BALI 4.4 and BALI 4.6 catamarans, are now in transit arriving in December and available for charters from December 14, 2024. BALI yachts are one of our most sought-after charter brands, making these new 2024 “Super Premier” catamarans an exciting addition to our Seychelles fleet. About the new BALI Catamarans The BALI 4.4 is a 44-foot 4-cabin/4-bath catamaran, perfect for families or groups of friends up to 10 people. The 5-cabin/4-bath BALI 4.6 is 46-feet, and is well-suited for larger groups or for allowing space for a hired skipper. Both yachts feature the popular “garage-door” style pivoting door that creates an open air salon that lends itself to comfortable indoor/outdoor living. Both yachts also feature spacious flybridge lounge areas for comfortable seating with a view while underway, or for sunset gatherings. Sailing the Seychelles Islands We began our first Dream Yacht charters in the Seychelles for good reason. This Indian Ocean Island chain is arguably one of the most beautiful sailing grounds on the planet, with 41 of the earth’s oldest granite islands and 74 low-lying islands surrounded by brilliant blue waters and pristine reefs. For nature lovers, the bird watching, hiking, and snorkeling are unmatched. And a visit to the protected island of Curieuse to observe the gentle giant Aldabra tortoises and unique coco de mer palms is a must. Underscoring Dream Yacht’s strong commitment to delivering top sailing opportunities in the beautiful Seychelles, we will welcome additional BALI yachts – 2 BALI 4.8 catamarans – in the Seychelles late in 2025. Plan now for your dream Seychelles sailing vacation to secure one of these stunning new sailing catamarans. Get in touch with a Dream Yacht charter planner today! Share: Link Copied to Clipboard
